# Cybersecurity source curation

Follow [the wiki blueprint](../../../wiki/README.md) and [the wiki content instructions](../../instructions/cybersecurity-wiki.instructions.md).

## Procedure

1. Confirm the user has selected the source for curation. Record its canonical title, authors or organisation, source type, publication/version date, original URL, and access date where available.
2. Check whether the source is open access and whether local capture is permitted. Preserve permitted captures under an appropriate `raw/` subdirectory and never edit an existing capture. For restricted sources, retain metadata and the URL plus notes based on material the user is authorised to provide; do not copy full text.
3. Read the source itself. Prefer the original paper, standard, official dataset documentation, or maintained software documentation over summaries. Clearly label secondary or vendor evidence.
4. Search existing wiki pages, aliases, and the source catalogue before creating anything. Resolve whether the source is a duplicate, a new version, or a genuinely new item.
5. Create or update one source page using the source template in the wiki blueprint. Extract only supported cybersecurity challenges, threat models, methods, data, evaluation, tools/providers, people, organisations, and dated developments.
6. Create or update only entities that add reusable knowledge. Link every source-derived claim back to the source page. Record quantitative results exactly as reported and keep limitations, uncertainty, and dual-use concerns visible.
7. Update relevant topic/index and timeline pages, plus the change log, if present. Do not create a synthesis from one source.
8. Validate frontmatter, required sections, provenance, local links, dates, licensing/access notes, and duplicate candidates. Summarise what changed and list any unresolved evidence gaps.

## Stop conditions

- Do not curate a source that the user has not selected for inclusion.
- Do not store an entire dataset or restricted/copyrighted full text in the repository.
- Do not fabricate missing source metadata, results, identities, licences, or tool status.
- Never delete, rename, or merge existing pages or raw captures without explicit user approval.
